sources.label: Dealroom — OpenAI publishes its internal pretraining curve and proposes industry-wide limits based on perplexity
TradingView / Seeking Alpha — OpenAI calls for industry-wide AI brake tied to perplexity

items.summary: OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki published the lab's internal log-perplexity curve from GPT-3.5 (~0.99) through GPT-4 (~0.91) to recent models below 0.8, and proposed that frontier labs agree on shared development limits — a first cap around the 0.68–0.70 window, where he expects further transformative capabilities — until monitoring tools such as a successor to chain-of-thought monitors catch up. He warns that AI-driven advances in pretraining research could arrive as an 'avalanche' as soon as 2027, and concedes perplexity is an imperfect yardstick: it is hard to compare across labs' datasets and misses gains from reasoning. The proposal lands as states move on the same question [[2026-11-19#7]], and it is a proposal, not a binding rule.
items.title: OpenAI publishes its pretraining perplexity curve and proposes industry-wide development limits

sources.label: SciBow — AI Just Wrote an Enzyme from Scratch. Here's Why That's a Big Deal

items.summary: El Nesr and colleagues report in Science the zero-shot de novo design of a working metalloenzyme, a catalyst evolution never produced. Their dEVA method — an evolutionary search in which LigandMPNN proposes mutations and Metal3D places metal ions — yielded desB, a TIM-barrel protein with a two-zinc active site that breaks down phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters with catalytic efficiency up to 1,500 M⁻¹s⁻¹ and a rate enhancement up to 3×10¹³ over the uncatalysed reaction. It needed no natural template, structure prediction or predefined motif, and the design emerged from only three experimentally tested candidates.
items.title: Zero-shot de novo design of a working metalloenzyme (dEVA) in Science

sources.label: National Governors Association — Governors Call for AI Action
FourWeekMBA — Governors' AI Plan Gives States 14 Principles, Washington 5

items.summary: The National Governors Association's bipartisan Governors Council — led by Wes Moore, Mike Braun, Josh Stein and Spencer Cox — issued 24 principles asking Congress for a risk-based federal framework for the most advanced general-purpose models, with independent audits and incident reporting, while keeping states as the primary accountability mechanism for AI harms to people. The principles urge caution on any federal preemption of state laws and call for clear, technically informed definitions of frontier models with regular review, without setting a compute threshold or reporting deadline. It is the governors' bid to shape the federal framework before Congress writes it.
items.title: US governors set out 24 AI principles: federal rules for frontier models, states keep harms

sources.label: Emergent — Kyutai AURA Model Streams Real-Time Avatars at 20.7 FPS

items.summary: Kyutai released AURA, an open-weight audio-driven avatar model that generates lip-synced talking-head video chunk by chunk from live audio, using a rolling KV cache and only the current audio chunk — no multi-second look-ahead. AURA 1.3B streams 576p video at 20.7 fps on a single GPU, running 23× faster than its bidirectional TalkVerse teacher, while AURA 5B streams 720p at 9.7 fps and matches the teacher's quality. Both weights ship with a dataset of 30,000 synthetic videos and teacher trajectories, plus a live browser demo.
items.title: Kyutai releases AURA, an open-weight streaming avatar model at 20.7 fps

sources.label: Business Standard — China's spies set sights on AI semiconductors years before Nvidia scandal (NYT)

items.summary: The New York Times reports that China's Ministry of State Security has run a covert campaign for at least two years to help Chinese companies acquire advanced AI chips and gather intelligence on the semiconductor supply chain, citing serving and former security officials in Asia, the US and Europe. A working group reporting directly to MSS chief Chen Yixin is said to help firms buy and smuggle restricted chips and to support Beijing's 'counter-blockade' work against US export controls [[2026-11-21#5]]. Beijing calls the espionage claims fabrication, and because the account rests on officials speaking anonymously, the scale of any smuggling remains unverified.
items.title: NYT: China's spy agency ran a two-year campaign to acquire advanced AI chips

sources.label: MarkTechPost — Columbia and CertiK Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels

items.summary: Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK introduced TensorLean, a Lean-based verifier that proves compiled GPU kernels match a tensor-level maths spec at the PTX level, checking data-race freedom, termination, output correctness within tolerance and untouched memory. Across 149 kernel instances — including every kernel of FlashAttention-2, -3 and -4 plus DeepGEMM — it proved 83 correct and found 38 bugs, 23 of them in FlashAttention, including a FlashAttention-4 data race that never appeared in 17,760 test runs. Specs run about 15× smaller than the kernel source, and checks take a median of about 10 minutes on a 16-core workstation.
items.title: TensorLean formally verifies GPU kernels at the PTX level, finds 38 bugs in FlashAttention and DeepGEMM

sources.label: arXiv — Efficient and Robust Drafting with Multi-Token Prediction

items.summary: Google researchers present G-MTP, an optimised multi-token prediction architecture that extends backbone LLMs to produce high-quality draft tokens for speculative decoding, where a drafter proposes tokens and the backbone verifies them in parallel. Tested on the Gemma 4 family, it delivers up to 3.1× speedups on large server-side setups and up to 2.3× on H100 for smaller models, with up to 2.2× on a smartphone GPU for on-device use. The work targets the drafting bottleneck directly, making faster inference a matter of better drafters rather than bigger verifiers.
items.title: G-MTP: multi-token prediction drafting speeds Gemma 4 inference up to 3.1×
